text:
nora: Quick follow-up from the dedicated-GPU-pools RFC review — a couple of subtle policy/ops edge cases we didn't lock down in the meeting. thinking about pre-warm vs burst, per-tenant min-reserved guarantees, and how strict binpacking should be when fragmentation is high. any quick takes?

ken: +1 on surfacing these. my gut: prefer soft guarantees (min-reserved) that are cheap to implement, and make pre-warm an opt-in for Tenants that pay for low-tail-latency.

maria: Concern: pre-warm can blow committed spend if not throttled. suggest pre-warm cap per-tenant and a global budget window (e.g., max_prewarm_gpu_per_minute, cooldown window). also need metrics: prewarm_root_cooling_seconds, prewarm_failures.

aj: Draft config idea (for autoscaler policy):
```yaml
policy_name: tenant_priority_scaler
min_nodes: 0  # reserved minimum per pool or tenant
min_reserved_per_tenant: 1  # can be 0 for free tier
target_utilization: 0.68
prewarm:
  enabled: true
  max_prewarm_per_tenant: 2
  warmup_seconds: 45
burst:
  enabled: true
  max_burst_nodes: 5
  billing_mode: "metered"  # or "reserve"
eviction_policy: "least_recent_job"  # soft eviction order
packing:
  strategy: "binpack_when_util_high"
  frag_threshold: 0.15  # if free capacity fragmentation > 15% trigger consolidation
fallback_priority: ["same_model_variant","compatible_variant","cheaper_variant"]
```

sam: couple of Qs: 1) When consolidation (binpacking) runs, do we preempt running in-progress requests? i hope not. 2) For burst nodes, are they in a separate tainted pool so scheduler doesn't assign long-running jobs?

ken: good points. consolidation should be gradual: only evict idle/pending workers. do not kill active endpoints with >0.2s left in their KV cache if the job is actively streaming. burst nodes = separate pool + shorter billing granularity + automatic node termination after N idle secs.

maria: +1 to separate tainted pool. also add a metric/alert: fractional_cost_increase due to prewarm/burst > 10% triggers audit. ops should be able to override per-account in Console.

autoscale-bot: [system] scale-up event: pool-dedicated-3 +2 gpus (reason: sustained queue depth > 60s, tenant=acme-inc, trigger=target_utilization breach)

nora: Implementation ACTIONS I see: 1) update RFC with config schema above and explicit semantics for eviction/consolidation (idle-only) 2) add sim harness that can run workload traces and show cost/latency deltas for prewarm/burst knobs 3) add Console UI toggles (prewarm cap, burst cap) + audit logs 4) add e2e canary (tenant-level) for 2 weeks before GA.

aj: I'll take the sim harness. will wire in a synthetic tail-latency trace and a multi-tenant poisson arrival model.

ken: I'll draft the eviction heuristics section and include the KV-cache safety rule (do not evict hosts with active KV hits in last 100ms).

maria: I'll spec the Console controls and the billing/budget guardrails.

nora: Cool. final note: we need an explicit downgrade path when a tenant toggles prewarm off (drain prewarmed nodes over a cooldown window, not immediate kill). put that in RFC. :thumbsup:

sam: minor: add a small blurb about region-aware routing (prefer cheaper region only when latency budget allows).

nora: good call. ok let's reconvene in 48h with PRs to the RFC draft. thanks all.
